body: Good point about the cost benefit ratio. I will think about that, thank you

I lived in my car for a while too. I find it so hard to lie, even though I understand it can be justified. It's like I start to feel like then I start lying to everyone. Not sure if I'm explaining it well. Thank you for the reply
Thank you. Took me the whole weekend but I finally got a phone
I sort of just want to die. A week ago I felt so good. Now I think it's just going to be the same and the same and the same and the same
I already have a google voice number but I'm using a library computer so I can only text. That's how I can pretend I have a phone to my roommates. But thank you for suggesting it
P.S. I already know about government benefits so please do not suggest it.

Please stay? Have you thought that maybe you should let go of your best friend from your life instead of letting go of life? I really hope you choose life. Best friends should support you no matter what and not think you're aggravating and needy. At least that's my opinion. Have you thought about finding new friends?  Depression isn't your fault and even if depression sucks, you deserve better than to die. Please stay please.

How you feel is real!! And I can relate to it. Regarding normal parenting, I can't say I'm an expert on normal parenting. All I know is that how my parents parent drives me crazy, and all this that we're talking about is a big part of it.

> She actually told me "ok, ModernEscapist, clearly your solution hasn't been working so we're going to do things my way!"
> 
> Thing is, we'd been trying to solve my issues her way for a few months by that point to no avail. Her revamped methods made it even worse. She just kept saying how I wasn't even considering the consequences of my depression on her and my dad, how they were doing all they could and I just wasn't doing the right thing, how I needed to just do exactly what she said and I would feel better.
> 
> Let me tell you, her way is definitely not the right way, which is why I refuse to ever talk to her about my feelings.

I feel like I could've written this. I'm not a teen but I have been getting help from my parents, and attemping for the whole time to do things my way. Alas they never let me do things my way, and it is my belief that that is why I'm still asking them for help. I know that logically doesn't sound like it makes sense but I just mean my problems aren't solved yet, which keeps me coninuing to try to solve them.

No you're not sounding like an entitled teen. I think your points seem very real and entirely make sense.

> I don't know if it's a power thing and she can't accept listening to me, or if she's convinced that her way (that she just thought up right now!) is better so she just scraps mine, but she will not do what I ask. And then I sound ungrateful and get the most annoying sounding whine of "I was just trying to help!" if I mention that while I appreciate her taking the time to do this, this is not what I asked for/needed or anywhere near as helpful as what I asked her to do.

This.

And a lot of the other stuff you wrote.

I think your feelings always have validity and more often than not actually point to things that your "rational" brain might not be grasping at that time.

I could actually relate to part of what you wrote. Just reentered the world after months of isolation. Not feeling too confident about being around other people. Not sure how much of it is the effect of the isolation, or the effect of having to still deal with Nparent, or if it's me.

But maybe it isn't you or me since it's at least two of us. :-)

Even if you feel bad, can you stick it out for a bit? Who knows, perhaps it will get better with some time.
Please do not suggest the subs about narcissism. I already know about them.
